methods.label: Pair the row counts
methods.explanation:
The total number of coins is
\[
S=1+2+\cdots+N.
\]
Write a second copy of this sum in reverse order. Pairing corresponding terms gives \(1+N\), \(2+(N-1)\), and so on. There are \(N\) pairs, each totaling \(N+1\), so
\[
2S=N(N+1).
\]
Since \(S=2016\), we need
\[
N(N+1)=4032.
\]
The consecutive integers \(63\) and \(64\) have this product:
\[
63\cdot64=4032.
\]
Thus \(N=63\). Adding another row always increases the total number of coins, so no other positive row count works. The requested digit sum is \(6+3=9\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: Derives the consecutive-integer sum formula through elementary pairing, then uses whole-number multiplication and place value.
